title: EAP, PEAP and authentication on the corporate network

videos.script: The last lesson ended with one password shared by everybody on the network. Everyone who knows it holds the same key, and anyone who leaves still has it. {{title}} A company network does it differently. Each person signs in with their own account, and a server decides who gets in. The standard is called 802.1X, and it works on cables as well as on Wi-Fi. {{server}} Each session then gets its own random key, so nobody can read a colleague's traffic, and switching off one account locks out one person. {{keys}} It has one weak point, and it sits on the laptop, not on the server. The laptop has to check that the server is really the company's before it hands over anything. {{check}} This lesson runs a real authentication in the lab, then points the same laptop at a fake server, configured properly and then carelessly.
